metadata.title: Politisk og demokratisk dannelse i en krisetid (ICCS 2022)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: ICCS 2022 is an international large-scale assessment implemented by IEA with complex sampling at multiple levels (students within schools, within countries). The book reports weighted results (e.g., “afrundede vægtede valide procentandele” and “vægtede valide procentandele”), indicating that analyses use survey weights to produce population-representative estimates within each participating country. The text also notes that some countries/regions did not meet IEA participation-rate standards and that Denmark’s school-level participation was affected by COVID-19, but quality checks indicate the Danish sample remains of high quality and generally representative. For replication or secondary analysis, analysts should use the official ICCS 2022 sampling weights provided in the IEA data products and apply the corresponding complex survey design features when estimating country-level percentages and scale scores.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This book primarily reports descriptive and comparative ICCS 2022 scale results (e.g., scale points and weighted percentages) rather than training predictive models on student-level outcomes. Plausible Values handling is therefore not applicable in the sense of a PV-based achievement prediction pipeline, because the reported outputs are not presented as model-based predictions from PVs. Missing-data handling is not reported at the level of an explicit analytic strategy (e.g., listwise/pairwise deletion or imputation) for an ML workflow, so the specific approach cannot be extracted from the provided text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The book reports international ICCS 2022 results based on responses from 14-year-old students in Grade 8 from 23 participating countries, and it provides Denmark-specific results based on 4,769 students in 249 classes across 134 schools. The text indicates that COVID-19 affected school participation in Denmark, leading to a lower school participation rate than the technical standard, but that quality analyses show the Danish sample is of high quality and generally meets representativeness criteria. No additional student-level inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., item nonresponse thresholds, complete-case rules, or PV-based analytic subsets) are specified in the provided excerpt.

data.outcome_summary: This volume reports descriptive and comparative findings from ICCS 2022, an IEA international assessment of civic and citizenship education among Grade 8 students (age 14) in 23 countries. The book uses weighted, valid percentages for many questionnaire items and reports scale scores in which the international mean is set to 50 (SD=10) for most attitude/identity scales, while some test scales use a different metric (e.g., 500/100). The cognitive test covers 121 items across domains such as institutions/systems, values/principles, interest/participation, and political/democratic identity; results are summarized as country means in scale points and as proportions of students at ICCS proficiency levels (A–E). The excerpt also documents COVID-19 impacts on administration and notes that Denmark’s school participation rate was below the technical standard, though quality checks suggest the sample remains representative. No predictive ML modeling, PV-based prediction pipeline, or explicit missing-data strategy is described in the provided text.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is for a descriptive comparative ICCS 2022 results book rather than an empirical ML paper. Consequently, there is no student-level predictive modeling target, no ML algorithm comparison, and no extractable PV/missing-data handling protocol tied to an ML workflow. The provided excerpt contains extensive scale and percentage reporting, but not the methodological details required to populate ML technique fields or PV/missing-data handling beyond the general ICCS reporting context.
